s1.title: Who is welcome here
s1.p1: Ágora is a community of people who build software: product, design, development and operations. There is no silly question, only questions without context.
s1.p2: You do not need to be an expert to answer. You do need to say where your experience comes from, so readers know how much weight to give it.
s1.p3: Disagreeing is part of the deal. Attacking the person instead of the argument is not.

s2.title: How to write a good topic
s2.p1: A specific title is worth more than ten lines of introduction. Compare: upload error against 403 error uploading an attachment larger than 5 MB.
s2.p2: Say what you already tried. Half of the answers we see are about things the person had already tested and did not mention.
s2.p3: Pick the right category and at most three tags. Too many tags is the same as none.

s3.title: Reports and what happens next
s3.p1: When you report something, write one line explaining what bothered you. Reports without context never reach the queue.
s3.p2: The team goes through the queue twice a day. Resolving takes the content offline; dismissing keeps the content and closes the case.
s3.p3: Every decision is kept in the history, with who reported it and when it was resolved.

s4.title: Muting, banning and coming back
s4.p1: The first broken guideline usually costs seven days of silence. A muted person keeps reading everything, but the reply box disappears.
s4.p2: The mute expires on its own. Nobody has to ask to come back.
s4.p3: Bans are for accounts created only to promote something and for people who repeat the same behaviour after two mutes.

s5.title: Reputation and badges
s5.p1: Reputation is not a number someone hands out: it comes from the votes your topics and replies received, with extra weight for the reply marked as the best one.
s5.p2: Badges are computed from thresholds. Ten replies, first best reply, one hundred reputation: each mark shows up on its own when you get there.
s5.p3: Downvotes exist and are not punishment. Use them for what is wrong, not for what you disagree with.

q1.q: Do I need an account to read the forum?
q1.a: No. All public content is open. An account is only needed to vote, reply and start a topic.

q2.q: Can I edit a reply after publishing it?
q2.a: Yes, at any time. The reply then shows the edited mark, so whoever already read it knows the text changed.

q3.q: Why does the best reply show up on top?
q3.a: Because people arriving from search want the solution, not the chronology. The original order stays right below, untouched.

q4.a: Whoever started the topic and the moderation team. Marking a reply as the best one also marks the topic as solved.

q5.a: You can ask the moderation team. We usually close instead of deleting when the topic already holds a useful answer for other people.

q6.a: In the lounge, yes, as long as you say the project is yours. Promotion disguised as a question is treated as spam.
